name: Event Organization Portal - SIA Project 21 22
description:
Information Systems - academic year 21/22
Course Project
Version 1.0.1 - 20/12/2021
Consider the following scenario:

A startup intends to develop a web portal that can help people who intend to organize an event, bringing together in a single website the information concerning the guests and the various services necessary for the event itself to take place.

The platform to be developed envisages the presence of providers and guests, in addition to the organizer.

At registration, providers supply, in addition to their credentials, their personal data and the data of the company they manage (VAT number, company address, accepted payment methods).

The provider, once registered, will be able to enter the services offered by their company, each belonging to a category (catering, hairdresser, florist etc.), each of which will be associated with a virtual showcase in which the provider can upload demonstration photos, together with the corresponding prices and the hours corresponding to the particular service shown by the showcase (e.g. Hairdresser's blow-dry service has as hours 10:00-12:00 from Tuesday to Thursday, Haircut + shampoo service with hours 8:00-12:00 + 15:00-18:00 from Tuesday to Saturday).

The event organizer, identified by their tax code, at registration, in addition to choosing their credentials, will provide their personal data, residence data and their IBAN for the possible payment of the services.

The organizer, through the portal, will be able to create the event, choosing the type of event (wedding, graduation, concert…) to organize, the date, the place where it will be held and the budget planned for the organization of the event. When creating the event the organizer will be able to choose from a pre-existing list the types of service for which they are interested in receiving help (for example catering, flowers, taxi service etc.).

The organizer will also be able to add the guests to the portal, entering the corresponding data, specifying, in addition to the personal data, the email with which the guest will be identified (and which they will use to log in) and the category to which the guest belongs (relative, friend, colleague etc.).

For each guest added, the system will generate an invitation code that will be sent by email to the specified address; this code will be used by the guest as a password to access the portal.

The organizer will also have available a blog associated with their event in which the organizer or the guests can write information about the event, post photos or videos and leave their thoughts by creating new posts or commenting on the existing ones.

The organizer, once the event has been created, will be able to view, for each service chosen when creating the event, the showcases of the providers that supply the chosen type of service and to arrange an appointment compatible with the hours observed by that service, specifying the details and any special requests. The provider, through their interface, will be able to view the various appointment requests and will have to approve them. The approved requests are displayed directly in a calendar on the site associated with the event, where the organizer will be able to consult the appointments for the agreed services.

After the meeting between the provider and the organizer (in which they agree on the details of the service), the provider calculates the quotation and proceeds to upload the amount on the portal, associating it with the completed appointment.

Once the upload has taken place the organizer can choose whether to accept or reject the quotation; if it is accepted, the total amount is subtracted from the remaining budget. By accepting the amount, the organizer chooses the payment mode (instalments, deposit + balance or full amount) and the payment method (online or on site). If the payment takes place on site the provider will proceed to confirm the amount paid through the portal (in the case of payment in several instalments the provider confirms the amount of each instalment received).

At any time the organizer will be able to consult the history of the contracts (with the related status and cost) and the budget balance for the entire event.
highLevelGoals: The Organizer aims to efficiently create, configure, and manage all aspects of an event, from initial setup to service selection and guest invitations.
The Organizer seeks to easily discover, compare, and book necessary services for their event, ensuring compatibility with their budget and schedule.
The Organizer wants to effectively invite guests, manage their information, and facilitate communication and interaction related to the event.
The Organizer aims to maintain clear visibility and control over the event's budget, quotations, and payment statuses.
The Provider aims to effectively present their services, including details, photos, prices, and availability, to potential Organizers.
The Provider seeks to efficiently receive, review, approve, and manage appointment requests from Organizers.
The Provider aims to easily generate and upload quotations, and confirm payments received for their services.
The Guest aims to easily access relevant information about the event they are invited to.
The Guest wants to participate in discussions, share thoughts, and view media related to the event through the event's blog.
lowLevelGoals: The Organizer can initiate the creation of a new event by providing a name and description.
The Organizer can specify the start and end dates and times for the event.
The Organizer can input the physical or virtual location details for the event.
The Organizer can upload an image to serve as the event's banner.
The Organizer can modify existing details of an event (e.g., name, description, date, location).
The Organizer can remove an event from the system.
The Organizer can view a list of all services offered by various Providers.
The Organizer can filter the list of services by specific categories (e.g., catering, photography, venue).
The Organizer can search for services using keywords.
The Organizer can access detailed information about a specific service, including description, images, and pricing.
The Organizer can send a request to a Provider for a quotation for a specific service for their event.
The Organizer can accept a received quotation from a Provider, initiating the booking process.
The Organizer can decline a received quotation from a Provider.
The Organizer can send event invitations to guests via email addresses.
The Organizer can view, add, or remove guests from the event's guest list.
The Organizer can monitor the RSVP status (accepted, declined, pending) of invited guests.
The Organizer can publish announcements or updates to the event's blog, visible to all guests.
The Organizer can access an overview of the event's total budget and current spending.
The Organizer can view the status of all requested and received service quotations (e.g., pending, accepted, declined).
The Organizer can check the payment status for booked services (e.g., pending, paid, partially paid).
The Provider can create a new service offering, including its name, description, and category.
The Provider can upload images to visually represent their service offering.
The Provider can define the pricing structure for their service (e.g., hourly rate, package price).
The Provider can update their availability calendar for their services.
The Provider can modify any existing details of their service offerings.
The Provider can delete a service offering from their showcase.
The Provider can see a list of all incoming appointment requests from Organizers.
The Provider can examine the details of a specific appointment request, including requested service, date, and Organizer information.
The Provider can accept an appointment request, confirming their availability.
The Provider can reject an appointment request, optionally providing a reason.
The Provider can propose an alternative date or time for an appointment.
The Provider can create a detailed quotation for a service based on an Organizer's request.
The Provider can upload a formal quotation document to the system for an Organizer.
The Provider can update the status of a quotation to 'sent' after it has been delivered to the Organizer.
The Provider can mark a payment for a booked service as received.
The Guest can access the event's name, description, date, time, and location.
The Guest can read announcements and updates posted by the Organizer on the event blog.
The Guest can accept or decline an event invitation.
The Guest can write and submit comments on the event's blog posts.
The Guest can read comments posted by other guests and the Organizer on the event's blog.
The Guest can upload images or videos to the event's blog.
The Guest can view images and videos shared by other guests and the Organizer on the event's blog.
